# SK2160 — The clock is read from a static

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A member reads DateTime.Now, DateTime.UtcNow, DateTime.Today or the DateTimeOffset equivalents from a static, so no caller and no test can give it a different time. Ships disabled; turn it on per path.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | none |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |
| Supersedes | S6354 |

## Why

A static clock read is a dependency the signature does not mention and the call site cannot replace. Code that depends on it can only be tested by waiting — which is what produces the `Thread.Sleep` that `SK8005` then reports — and by tests that pass in one time zone and fail in another. `TimeProvider`, .NET 8's answer, turns the read into an ordinary injected dependency: the test supplies the instant and the production path supplies `TimeProvider.System`.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
public bool IsExpired(Token token) => token.ExpiresAt < DateTime.UtcNow;
```

Write:

```csharp
public bool IsExpired(Token token) => token.ExpiresAt < time.GetUtcNow();
```

## When it does not fire

MEASUREMENT-PENDING

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2160.severity (`none` by default; set it per path to enable)`
